question.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -6 & 5\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}+\,\,\frac{1}{9}$ $30t-26$ .
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]{e}^{3t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & {e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{-t} & 3{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}\cdot 3{e}^{3t}-{e}^{3t}\cdot {e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2{e}^{2t}}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{3t} & -{e}^{3t} \\ -{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ -{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ -t{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ -t{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -t{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(3t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot (3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =3t{e}^{t}-3{e}^{t} \\  & =3{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -t{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t & =(-t)\cdot (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t})-\int (-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{-3t})\cdot (-\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{t}{3}{e}^{-3t}-\frac{1}{3}\int {e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{t}{3}{e}^{-3t}+\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}(3t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & {e}^{3t} \\ {e}^{-t} & 3{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t}(t-1) \\ \frac{1}{9}{e}^{-3t}(3t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}27(t-1)+(3t+1) \\ 27(t-1)+3(3t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}30t-26 \\ 36t-24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
